procedural_matters: GER 875 was represented by Moritz Dorau. ESP 5 was represented by Conrad Konitzer. Benjamin Bildstein the coach of GER attended the hearing as an observer. NED 987 represented by Robbert HUISMAN gave evidence as a witness for GER 875.
facts: GER 875 and ESP 5 both sailing downwind on starboard tack.
ESP 5 clear ahead and to windward of GER 875 with the lateral distance of 150 metres between the boats.
ESP 5 gybed on port tack on the converging course with GER 875.
When distance between the boats was half a boat length, and GER 875 was pointing in the middle of the ESP 5's wing GER 875 luffed sharply.
While the boat was capsizing, a crew member fell onto the boat and injured.
ESP 5 retired from the race no. 5 after finished the race.
The crew member has sustained injuries; he has damaged his right leg and he is still under medical observation.
conclusions: ESP 5 on port tack failed to keep clear of GER 875 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.

GER 875 score in race 5 was made significantly worse through no fault of her own by injury because of the action of ESP 5 that broke a RRS 10 and took the appropriate penalty. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(2) as changed by RRS B5.61.4 are met.
decision: The protest is upheld. Since ESP 5 took an applicable penalty, she is not further penalized under RRS 60.5(c)(2). Redress is given to GER 875. GER 875 is to be scored in race 5 points equal to the average, rounded to the nearest tenth of a point (0.05 to be rounded upward), of her points in races no. 4 and no. 5. No other boat’s score shall change.
